body.statement: For every \(t\in[0,1]\), the robust region \(\mathcal R_t\) is relatively downward closed on its target-existence domain: whenever two budget pairs are coordinatewise ordered, the larger lies in \(\mathcal R_t\), and the target exists at the smaller, the smaller lies in \(\mathcal R_t\).  Whenever the fixed observed mass array is rational, the region has a finite piecewise-algebraic boundary obtained from the chart in \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}rational\text{-}charts}\).  The chart separately labels the falsification boundary, the positive-\(H\) target-existence boundary, and the conclusion boundary \(L=t\).
body.justification: Separating incompatibility, an empty target stratum, and failure of the benefit conclusion prevents three substantively different robustness failures from being conflated.
body.gap: Masten and Poirier and Picchetti study breakdown frontiers where the target remains defined across the maintained region; survivor-complier mass introduces a distinct existence frontier.
body.consumer: An analyst can report the weakest joint monotonicity relaxations under which a stated minimum fraction of always-selected compliers benefits.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\delta'=(\delta'_D,\delta'_S)\) and \(\delta=(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) satisfy \(\delta'\leq\delta\) coordinatewise.  Every constraint other than the two budgets is unchanged.  Because \(f_x,c_x\geq0\), enlarging either budget weakens its corresponding inequality.  Hence
\[
 \bigcup_oQ_o(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_oQ_o(q;\delta_D,\delta_S),
\]
and, after restricting to \(H>0\),
\[
 \Theta_I(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 \subseteq
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]
Suppose the target exists at \(\delta'\) and \(\delta\in\mathcal R_t\).  Endpoint attainment gives
\[
 L(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 =\min\Theta_I(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 \geq\min\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\geq t.
\]
Thus \(\delta'\in\mathcal R_t\), proving relative downward closure.  Requiring existence at the smaller pair is essential because compatibility itself expands, rather than contracts, with the budgets.

On each target-nonempty stratum supplied by the finite-rational-chart theorem, write \(L=A/B\) with the sign of the nonzero denominator \(B\) fixed.  The condition \(L\geq t\) is then one polynomial weak inequality, obtained by multiplying by the recorded sign of \(B\).  It follows that \(\mathcal R_t\) is a finite union of semialgebraic chart pieces.  Its boundary is contained in the finite union of chart boundaries and the algebraic equality pieces \(A-tB=0\), so it is finite piecewise algebraic.  The exact chart certificates distinguish: absence of every feasible branch, which is the falsification label; feasible branches with \(H=0\) at every vertex, which is the target-existence label; and positive-denominator pieces on which \(A-tB=0\), which is the conclusion label \(L=t\).  Intersections may carry more than one label, but the three causes are not conflated.
